input.query: I need to explain a new cooperative board game to beginners. Which retrieved guidance helps me decide the order of the explanation?

items.text: This facilitator note covers the explanation order for introducing a new cooperative board game. The event uses four tables, each with one copy of the same game. Participants arrive with different experience levels, so each table has a printed card that repeats the same few rules. The organizer reserves the first part of the session for introductions and asks the helpers to leave technical exceptions until a participant encounters one. Helpers collect coats away from the tables, place unused pieces in a tray and leave a clear area for the first demonstration. The materials list includes pencils, a timer, one score sheet per table, spare cards, labels for the boxes and a large card showing how a round ends. These logistical details are useful to the event staff but are not the rules explanation itself. During the briefing, helpers take turns reading the short opening aloud and checking whether a newcomer can identify the goal. Each helper then practices a sample turn with another helper watching silently. The observer writes down any word that requires a definition. The briefing ends with a reminder to keep the game’s final objective visible while participants make their first moves. The explanation itself should follow this order: first state the shared objective, then demonstrate one ordinary turn, then show the condition that ends the round. Ask one participant to describe what they would do on their first turn. Only then introduce an exception if it is relevant to the pieces currently on the table.
